history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row ('Gayatri Shaktipeeth (Chamunda Mata Temple)', Ajmer) describes the same temple as seq 2057 (Chamunda Mata Temple, Taragarh) - the hilltop Chamunda shrine on the Aravalli ridge behind the main Taragarh peak near Ajmer; kept as a separate file per the one-file-per-row rule. It sits at about 600 m above sea level with views of the Nagpahar hills, the fissure and Ana Sagar lake. It is the principal Devi shrine of Ajmer and the kuldevi of the Chauhan dynasty. Local tradition (kivandati) says an ancestor of Prithviraj Chauhan built it about 1200 years ago and that Vigraharaj IV (Bisaldeo Chauhan) renovated it, walking daily from his fort to worship; legend says the goddess presented him her sword (khadag) and he remained unmarried and built a great Chauhan empire. These age, builder and daily-worship claims are local legend and should be treated as unverified. Devotees throng through the year, peaking at Navratri. Coordinates below are approximate: they are the map-listed temple address near Foy Sagar; the exact hilltop shrine position could not be verified (verify).

name: Gayatri Shaktipeeth (Chamunda Mata Temple)
town: Ajmer (on the hill behind Taragarh, near Foy Sagar)
town_description: Ajmer, in central Rajasthan, is one of the state's oldest cities - founded by Chauhan king Ajaypal, seat of the Chauhan dynasty, home to the Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, Taragarh Fort, Ana Sagar lake and the Jain pilgrimage centre of Soniji Ki Nasiyan. It is a major rail junction and a gateway to the pilgrimage town of Pushkar, 15 km away.

travel.railway: Ajmer Junction railway station - city transport buses are reported to run from the station towards the temple (verify).
travel.road: Taragarh hill near Foy Sagar lake, Ajmer; reach by taxi/auto from the city, then a climb (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; August monsoon greenery is also praised (verify).
